# Apocalypse of Peter — Chapter 1
**Agent:** LOGOS (Formal Equivalence)
**Source:** Akhmim Fragment / Ethiopic MS, Apocalypse of Peter 1

---

1. While he was seated upon the Mount of Olives, his own disciples approached him. We were beseeching him individually and imploring him, saying to him: "Show us what the signs of your coming will be and of the end of the age."

2. Our Lord answered and said to us: "Take care that no one deceives you. Many will come in my name, saying, 'I am the Christ.' Do not believe them, and do not go near them.

3. For deceivers and false prophets will arise, and they will establish teachings and various doctrines, ensnaring those who are on the path to destruction.

4. These shall be sons of perdition. Then God, my Father, shall come to raise the dead, to judge the living and the dead, and to reward each person according to their works."

5. He showed us in his right hand the souls of all people, and in the palm of his right hand the image of what will come to pass in the last day.

6. And I saw how the wicked were given over to the angels of punishment, who drove them toward a place of outer darkness.

7. He said to us: "When the fig tree has put forth its shoots, in the last days deceivers and false prophets will arise and will teach various doctrines, ensnaring those who are perishing.

8. As for the parable of the fig tree — understand it in this way: when its shoots have sprung up and its branches have grown, the end of the world will come."

9. I, Peter, answered and said to him: "Interpret for me the parable of the fig tree as well. How shall we understand it?"

10. The Lord answered me and said: "Do you not understand that the fig tree is the house of Israel? It is like a man who planted a fig tree in his garden. It produced no fruit, and he looked for fruit on it for many years. Finding none, he said to the keeper of his garden: 'Uproot this fig tree, that it may not render our ground unfruitful.'

11. The keeper of the garden said to him: 'Allow us to remove it once more, to dig around it and water it; and if it does not bear fruit we will immediately remove its roots from the garden and plant another tree in its place.'

12. Have you not understood that the fig tree is the house of Israel? Truly I say to you, when its branches have sprouted in the last days, false Christs will come and stir up hope, saying, 'I am the Christ, who has now come into the world.'

13. And when they see the wickedness of their deeds — those of the false Christs — they will turn away and follow them, denying the one to whom our fathers gave praise, the first Christ whom they crucified and thereby sinned greatly.

14. But this deceiver is not the Christ. And when they reject him, he will kill with the sword, and there will be many martyrs."

15. Then the branches of the fig tree — that is, the house of Israel — will shoot forth; and there will be many martyrs by his hand, killed and becoming martyrs.

16. "Enoch and Elijah will be sent to instruct them that this is the Deceiver who must come into the world to perform signs and wonders in order to deceive.

17. And therefore those who die at his hand will be martyrs and will be counted among the good and righteous martyrs who have pleased God throughout their lives."

---
*LOGOS follows the formal structure of the Akhmim Greek, with preference for clause-level equivalence. Tense and mood rendered as precisely as English allows.*
